stem: A 25-year-old patient has malaria confirmed by blood microscopy. Testing shows anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated bilirubin. In a hypothetical observation of infected red cells, investigators record a burst of merozoites and hemozoin into the surrounding fluid. Which of the following events most directly explains that burst?

options.label: A
options.text: Rupture of infected erythrocytes into extracellular fluid
options.explanation: Lysis of infected erythrocytes releases merozoites and hemozoin. This directly matches both the observed cellular compartment and the simultaneous appearance of these materials outside it.
options.misconception: No misconception: Rupture of infected red cells explains the sudden extracellular appearance of their contents.

options.label: B
options.text: Attachment of intact erythrocytes to vascular lining
options.explanation: Endothelial adherence is relevant to falciparum sequestration, but attachment of intact cells does not itself explain the observed burst of material from within infected erythrocytes.
options.misconception: Confuses adherence of an intact infected cell with release of material from inside it.

options.label: C
options.text: Retention of parasite products within intact red cells
options.explanation: Retention would keep the measured products inside the cell. The experiment instead observes their sudden appearance in surrounding fluid, requiring a release event.
options.misconception: Uses intracellular retention to explain products observed outside the infected cells.

options.label: D
options.text: Transfer of extracellular products into uninfected red cells
options.explanation: This describes movement into cells rather than the observed movement out of infected cells. It therefore reverses the direction of the measured release event.
options.misconception: Reverses the measured direction of movement by describing entry into cells rather than release.

options.label: E
options.text: Continued parasite growth within infected erythrocytes
options.explanation: Growth within an intact boundary does not account for the recorded burst into surrounding fluid. The defining event in this observation is infected-cell lysis.
options.misconception: Equates parasite growth inside an intact cell with the observed burst of extracellular material.

context: Learning objective: connect the symptomatic blood stage of malaria to rupture of infected erythrocytes. Release of parasite products from these cells links the intracellular stage to the observed extracellular material.
